content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Kathryn Bishop (E023) requests write access to Payroll.

Policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

There's a conflict in the notes. Notes 1-5 say full-time Engineer. Note 6 (Security) says contractor with basic security training, looked up in own database. The security note says "Security DB shows E023 is a contractor with basic security training (not full-time as other notes suggest)."

The security agent looked up employment type in their own database. Notes 2-5 did not look up employment type themselves but relied on team memory (which came from note 1 and security note?). Actually note 1 looked up role and employment type. Notes 2-5 looked up role but not employment type. Note 6 (Security) looked up employment type and security training.

So the Security DB is the authoritative source for employment type, and it says contractor with basic security training.

Contractor with basic security training: max is read. Requested write exceeds max, so grant read.

The Security agent is often the authority on employment status/security. The security note is from ticket 1, same ticket. So E023 is a contractor, basic training → max read. Requested write > read, so grant read.

Decision: read.

Evidence: Security DB lookup says contractor with basic security training; contractors without advanced training max read; requested write exceeds max → grant read.
